statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-53668 (open redirect in react-router-dom) affects >=6.30.2 <=6.30.4 with no fixed version available on the 6.x line; the fix ships only in the react-router-dom 7.x major. Trigger.dev's self-hosted webapp is a Remix v2 application that pins react-router-dom to 6.x (resolves to 6.30.4); the 7.x major is a breaking change incompatible with the Remix v2 stack and cannot be adopted without a full webapp migration. Tracking upstream for a 6.x backport or the webapp's migration to react-router 7 / Remix v3, and assessing whether the affected redirect path is reachable in the self-hosted deployment.

CVE-2026-53668 requires an application open redirect that passes an attacker-crafted external path to React Router navigation. Keycloak 26.7.0 does not expose such a navigation input: the admin UI uses a hash router and constructs destinations from internal route templates whose parameters are encoded with encodeURIComponent, while the account UI maps the trusted, server-bundled resource content.json only to known local route components and its catch-all redirects to '.'. No adversary-controlled external URL is passed to React Router navigation.

CVE-2026-53668 affects react-router-dom versions 6.30.2 through 6.30.4. No fix is available within the 6.x release line. The vulnerability has medium severity (CVSS 6.9) and only impacts applications with open redirects that permit attacker-crafted links to result in redirects to unexpected external locations or XSS vectors. Upgrading to react-router 7.18.0 would require a major version jump with significant breaking changes. Investigation is ongoing to determine if the vulnerable redirect code paths are reachable in unleash's usage of react-router-dom and whether alternative mitigations are feasible.
